text: Robert C. Harvey (May 31, 1937 – July 7, 2022) was an American author, critic, and cartoonist known for his work on the history and theory of cartooning, with a particular focus on the comic strip. He worked as a freelance cartoonist and described drawing cartoons since age 7. He earned a B.A. from the University of Colorado, where he submitted cartoons to the campus humor magazine, The Flatiron. After graduating in 1959, he tried to make a living as a freelance cartoonist in New York but was interrupted by service in the U.S. Navy from 1960 to 1963, during which he served as paymaster aboard the USS Saratoga. Upon discharge, he taught high school English for five years (1964–1969) before working for 30 years as a convention manager for the National Council of Teachers of English. He obtained a Master's Degree in English from New York University in 1968 and a Ph.D. in English literature from the University of Illinois Urbana-Champaign in 1978. While at NCTE, he freelanced cartoons to magazines from 1978 to 1982. In 1973, he began writing about comics and cartooning for The Menomonee Falls Gazette, and in 1976, his columns started appearing in The Comics Journal, where he had a regular column. During the 1990s, Fantagraphics Books published two volumes of Cartoons of the Roaring Twenties, collected and edited by Harvey. He also contributed biographies of several cartoonists to Oxford University Press' American National Biography. In 1994, his first work of comics scholarship, The Art of the Funnies, was published by the University Press of Mississippi, followed by The Art of the Comic Book in 1996. He served as an associate editor for the journal Inks: Cartoon and Comic Art Studies, handling submissions related to the comic strip. In 1998, Harvey was guest curator for the Children of the Yellow Kid exhibition at the Frye Museum in Seattle, for which he also provided the catalogue. Harvey authored or edited thirteen books on comics and cartooning, including Milton Caniff: Conversations (2002) from the University Press of Mississippi, followed by a full biography of Caniff, Meanwhile... A Biography of Milton Caniff, Creator of Terry and the Pirates and Steve Canyon (2007) published by Fantagraphics. His most recent book is Insider Histories of Cartooning: Rediscovering Forgotten Famous Comics and Their Creators (2014) from the University Press of Mississippi. A complete list of his books is available on his website. He interviewed cartoonists for the long-running quarterly magazine Cartoonist PROfiles and contributed a column briefly to the Comics Buyer's Guide. Harvey was a member of the National Cartoonists Society and an associate member of the Association of American Editorial Cartoonists. He received awards including the All-Navy Cartoonist in 1960, the AAEC Ink Bottle Award in 2013 "in recognition of dedicated service to the Association and distinguished efforts to promote the art of editorial cartooning," and the San Diego Comic-Con's Inkpot Award in 2018 "for achievement in comic arts." He married his wife Linda née Kubicek in 1971 and had twin daughters, Julia (Jill) and Katherine (Kit), born in May 1975. In late June 2022, Harvey fell and unknowingly broke six ribs; he was hospitalized and died from complications of the fall on July 7, 2022, at the age of 85.
